The area of $ABCD$ is $34{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$   What is the area of $△BCD$ rounded to the nearest integer?

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946476/assets/33aff6da54b72146f89bbd580a889a4050bff89bca86ddb6b74b80f62875a470.png)

The area of $ABCD$ is $5{\text{ km}}^{2}.$   Then, the area of $△BCD$, rounded to the **nearest integer**, is{{field-1}}${\text{km}}^{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's start by finding the area of $△ABD.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot AD\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2.5\cdot 6\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{63}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 15\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{63}^{∘} \\  & =6.682… \\  & ≈7{\text{ km}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the **nearest integer**.

The difference of the areas of $△ABD$ and the quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives the area of $△BCD.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△BCD} & ={A}_{△ABD}-{A}_{ABCD} \\  & =7-5 \\  & =2{\text{ km}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
